replaced_prose.original: \autoref{interlude-execution-unit} traces how that execution unit later changed.
replaced_prose.replacement: \autoref{interlude-execution-unit} traces the architectural progression from whole-document execution through page chunking to skeletonized residency.

replaced_prose.original: \caption{\emph{Two execution units for document remediation.} (a) Whole-document execution keeps the artifact\textquotesingle s working state and media resident in one long-running worker. (b) Page-chunked execution divides the document across workers, reducing the working state and memory required by any one worker.}
replaced_prose.replacement: \caption{\emph{Three stages of DocAble\textquotesingle s document processing architecture.} (a) Initially, one worker retained the complete document, including its media. (b) Page chunking reduced the working set per worker, but each chunk still retained its media. (c) Skeletonization separated document structure from media, retaining only structure and references in worker memory while streaming media on demand. Chunking changed the execution unit; skeletonization changed the residency requirement.}

replaced_prose.original: Implementation eventually supplies measurements to compare with the model’s predictions. A residual --- the gap between prediction and observation --- turns into an engineering question, and it drives a loop that runs both before and after implementation (\autoref{interlude-prediction-residual}).
replaced_prose.replacement: Implementation eventually supplies measurements to compare with the model’s predictions. A residual --- the gap between prediction and observation --- turns into an engineering question. \autoref{interlude-prediction-residual} connects the general engineering loop in panel a to an illustrative prediction error in panel b and the refinement of the model in panel c.

replaced_prose.original: \caption{\emph{Using prediction error as evidence.} (a) The gap between a model\textquotesingle s prediction and the observed measurement is a residual, pointing to a wrong parameter, a wrong relation, or a missing mechanism; the numbers are illustrative. (b) Prediction and measurement create a feedback loop: explain the residual, refine the model, and test the revised model against subsequent observations.}
replaced_prose.replacement: \caption{\emph{Modeling through prediction and measurement.} (a) An engineering problem motivates a model whose analysis informs implementation. Measurements test its predictions and may require the model to be revised. (b) A discrepancy between predicted and observed latency directs investigation toward an incorrect parameter, an incorrect relationship, or a missing mechanism. The numerical values are illustrative. (c) The revised model is tested again until its residual is acceptable for the question being investigated.}

scope: Two figure consolidations only. Execution partitioning and media residency remain independent; prediction values are illustrative; panel c concerns model refinement.

inventory.caption: *Chunked residency versus skeletonized residency.* (a) Page chunking limits how much document state and associated media a worker holds at once, but media remains part of the worker's resident representation. (b) Skeletonization keeps only document structure and media references resident. Individual media objects stream from external storage to the consumer on demand, so total media size no longer determines persistent worker memory.
inventory.conversion: TikZ diagram; inspect SVG and chapter/receipt
inventory.svg_description:
Two panels. (a) Chunked, format-native representation: an OOXML document is split into
    page chunks, and each of several workers holds its chunk's structural state together with the media for
    that chunk, so media remains part of the worker's resident representation. (b) Skeletonized
    representation: the OOXML document becomes a structural skeleton plus media references held by the
    worker, while media stays in an external store and individual media objects stream to the GenAI service
    on demand. Total media size no longer determines persistent worker memory.

inventory.svg_title: Modeling as a loop, not a linear documentation step
inventory.svg_description:
Two panels. (a) The process is not linear — design, then implement, then document with
    models. (b) It can be a loop: a problem drives a model; analyzing the model yields a prediction and a
    design; those drive implementation and then measurement; measurement refines the model, and the loop
    continues while the questions justify the cost.
